thread.title: Spotify's stock indicated at $150 to $160 or higher--as it kicks off unorthodox 'direct listing' - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Spotify's stock indicated at $150 to $160 or higher--as it kicks off unorthodox 'direct listing' - MarketWatch
text:
Global music-streaming giant Spotify Technology SA SPOT, +14.11% made its debut on the New York Stock Exchange Tuesday afternoon. The company is using a so-called direct-listing process. That means it will let existing shares float publicly without offering any new shares on an exchange and without an underwriting bank to help buoy its stock price in the open market. Why? Spotify wanted to democratize the process and they didn't need to raise fresh money through the offering as is often the case with an IPO. Spotify kicked off trade at $165.90 and was down more than 6% at $155.42 in recent action, after hanging around a range between $167 to $170, as holders of the stock tried to arrive at a price. So-called designated market makers Citadel Securities will help to ensure that the process is orderly by helping facilitate trading throughout the session . Morgan Stanley is serving as the lead adviser to Spotify. Spotify's stock initially had a reference price of $132, which was the basis for open bidding. Based on that price shares of Spotify are up more than 20%. Competitors to Spotify include Pandora Media Inc. P, -3.03% which is trading down 2.4% and has declined 3% so far in 2018. That compares with a decline of 3.5% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.33% and a year-to-date loss of 2.9% for the S&P 500 index SPX, +1.06% Apple Inc.'s AAPL, +0.67% music-streaming business and Amazon.com Inc.'s AMZN, +1.79% are also viewed as competitors to the Stockholm-based Spotify, which officially launched its business in 2008.
